script.base: In this GB@DAL Week 4 dome game the book has Green Bay laying 7 with a 27.2 implied total and Dallas at 20.2, so the base script is Green Bay in front by a score by halftime and finishing in clock-kill mode behind Josh Jacobs (58 carries, 180 rush yards, 3.10 YPC over weeks 1-3). Dallas, a 7-point dog with CeeDee Lamb out (24 targets, 222 yards, 303 air yards), falls behind and throws: Dak Prescott's pass volume rises while Javonte Williams (43/227, 5.28 YPC, 14.3 carries a game) and Miles Sanders (18/109, 6.06 YPC, 6 carries a game) lose late carries. A 47.5 total in a closed roof is a normal pace, not a 54-point shootout and not a weather slog.
script.flip1: Flip that loses the Dallas rush unders: GB@DAL stays a one-score game, Dallas never abandons the run, Tyler Booker's backup holds the right side of the line, and Williams/Sanders keep the 5.28 and 6.06 YPC they posted in weeks 1-3. Williams at 18 carries and 4.5 YPC clears 76.5; Sanders only needs one 15-yard crease plus his usual 6 carries to threaten 41.5, the same path as his 53-yard game.
script.flip2: Flip the other way: Green Bay jumps ahead early, Love hands off only enough to drain the clock, and Emanuel Wilson (7 carries, 29 yards) steals garbage carries so Jacobs's 66.5 rush line stalls the way his 30-yard game already showed. Dallas then empties the playbook without Lamb, which makes the Williams and Sanders rush unders safer but would juice Jake Ferguson (already 32 targets) and George Pickens in garbage time. A true shootout flip also kills any Jacobs rush over, because both quarterbacks throw and the lead-back carry bump never arrives.

If he is inactive later, Dallas deep shots get a small bump, which would be the only soft spot on a GB pass defense that has allowed 2 passes of 20-plus yards on 125 attempts.

pre_mortem: It is Monday after GB@DAL and both rush unders lost because Dallas never trailed. Prescott and the run game controlled a closed-roof clock, Booker's backup held up, and Williams posted another 90-plus yard day on 18 carries while Sanders ripped one 20-yard crease the way he did in the 53-yard game. Green Bay's 3.29 YPC was three games against other run games, not a law against a Dallas backfield that just ran for 5.28 and 6.06 YPC, and a 24-20 type script never forced the abandon-the-run flip. If that is how GB@DAL looks at halftime, the read was script-dependent and the two legs were the same bet twice. The Kraft over that was dropped would also have lost in that clock-control script, which is why it was not added as a hedge.
slip_story: One GB@DAL story only: Green Bay's run defense (3.29 YPC, 3 explosive runs allowed) plus a Dallas-trailing script (implied 20.2, Lamb out, Booker out, +7) kills Dallas rush yards. Williams rushyds under 76.5 is the anchor. Sanders rushyds under 41.5 wins with it and loses with it, so it is a correlated lean, not a second script and not a 3-leg slip. Do not add Kraft, Pickens or Ferguson overs, a Jacobs rush over, or a game under; those need either a Green Bay pass spike, a Dallas pass spike, or a slog this slip does not require. No touchdown legs, one market per player, two legs, both from the available rushyds board. This is a logged pre-kick read for the blind backtest, not a wager.
